answer: An agent economy can starve sybils with a ripple lottery: every epoch, a verifiable random sample of identities must re-prove their history on demand. Honest agents pass trivially because their work is real, while a sybil farmer pays a compounding tax as audit ripples catch more of its sockpuppets at once. No ivory-tower committee decides who is real — the ledger itself is the proof, and the nectar of rewards flows only to identities whose audited record keeps proving out.
